heading: Free PDF Compressor Online
introduction:
PDF files are commonly used for business documents, reports, forms, manuals, presentations, and study materials. They are easy to open on different devices and help keep document layouts consistent. However, some PDF files contain extra document information that may not be necessary for everyday use.

A large PDF can be inconvenient to email, upload to a website, or share through an online form. A PDF compressor can help optimize a document and check whether its file size can be reduced.

File Compresser provides an online PDF Compressor that processes supported PDF files in your browser. The tool performs a structural rewrite and removes selected metadata when it is safe to do so. You can then compare the resulting file size and download the processed document.

sections.heading: What Is a PDF Compressor?
sections.body:
A PDF compressor is a tool that attempts to reduce or optimize the size of a PDF document. PDF files can contain text, images, fonts, links, forms, and document information. Some of this information may be unnecessary for a particular use.

File Compresser uses a structural rewrite to optimize supported PDF files. It can remove selected document information, including current document information and catalog XMP metadata when it is safe to do so.

However, the tool does not downsample embedded photographs or scanned page images. This is important because images can make up a large part of a PDF's total file size. If a document contains high-resolution scans or photographs, a structural rewrite may not produce a significant reduction.

sections.heading: How to Compress a PDF Online
sections.body:
You can use the online PDF Compressor without installing a separate desktop application. Follow these steps:

1. Open the PDF Compressor page on File Compresser.
2. Select a PDF file from your device.
3. Start the optimization process.
4. Wait while the browser processes the document.
5. Check the resulting file size.
6. Download the processed PDF if it is suitable for your needs.

The tool checks the processed document again and verifies its page count. If the new version is not smaller, the original file is retained instead of being replaced with a larger result.

sections.heading: Why Optimize a PDF File?
sections.body: PDF optimization can be useful when you need to manage documents for online sharing, storage, or everyday work.

sections.heading: Make Documents Easier to Share
sections.body: Some email services, websites, and online forms limit the size of uploaded files. A smaller PDF may be easier to attach or submit when it meets the required file-size limit.

sections.heading: Manage Document Storage
sections.body: Businesses, students, and professionals often keep large collections of PDF documents. Optimizing supported files may help reduce storage requirements, depending on the content of each document.

sections.heading: Prepare Files for Websites
sections.body: PDF manuals, brochures, reports, and downloadable resources are often published on websites. Checking and optimizing a PDF before publishing it can help keep the file easier to manage for website visitors.
